findings.where: "Where we're starting" section: the Canggu, Uluwatu and Kuta Lombok destination cards and their "Best hostels" lines with chevrons; this is also where the hero's "Explore destinations" button and the nav's "Destinations" link send visitors
findings.fault: The three cards look clickable but do nothing. Each is a white raised card with a border, a shadow and a hover rule, and each has a "Best hostels" line in link colour with a chevron. None of them is a link. Sending visitors to the destination guides is one of this page's three jobs. Every route to the guides on the page ends at these cards, so a visitor can't reach any guide.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker who taps "Explore destinations" or a card's "Best hostels" to see Canggu hostels. Nothing happens, so the site looks broken or empty before launch, and there is no other way to reach the guides.

findings.where: Nav "How we rank"; footer "How we rank", "Privacy", "Terms" and "Report content"
findings.fault: These links are dead. Each one points back to this same page, so clicking it takes the visitor nowhere new. The ranking method is the page's main promise of trust, and the privacy policy is what someone checks before handing over an email address. Neither can be reached.
findings.who_objects: A traveller checking the "merit alone" claim before trusting the ranking, or checking the privacy policy before emailing for launch news. They click, nothing new loads, and the page looks unfinished or evasive.

findings.where: Hero: the coral "Email luc@mantahostels.com for launch news" button
findings.fault: The page's main action is a mailto link styled as a button. On a phone without a mail app set up (many travellers use webmail), the tap opens nothing or an unwanted setup screen. When it does work, the visitor gets a blank email and has to work out what to write. The button looks like a one-step sign-up, but it hands the visitor a task.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker on a phone who wants launch news. Their tap does nothing or opens a mail app they don't use, so the page's one contact-collecting action is lost.

findings.where: Desktop nav bar: "Destinations" against "How we rank"
findings.fault: The two nav links have different treatments. "How we rank" is underlined at rest and "Destinations" is not. The underline suggests that one is the current page or a different kind of link, but neither is the current page. The project's rules mark the current page with semibold, not an underline.
findings.who_objects: A visitor reading the nav, who may take "How we rank" as the current page or as different in kind from "Destinations". It's a small confusion that most visitors will get past.
